strengths: Sound technical approach that appropriately adapts existing graph self-supervised learning methods to RTL quality estimation, with well-motivated design choices such as masking post-GNN embeddings to preserve computational integrity

Comprehensive experimental evaluation with large-scale dataset (13,200 designs), strong baselines including recent LLM-based methods, informative ablation studies, and consistent improvements across multiple metrics
Clear presentation with good motivation, informative figures, and thorough methodology description; addresses a practically important problem in EDA workflows
Appropriate handling of class imbalance through stratified masking and class-balanced focal loss, addressing a key challenge in CDFG-based learning
weaknesses: Limited novelty: primarily applies existing techniques (GraphMAE, MaskGAE, class-balanced focal loss, spectral positional embeddings) to a new domain without substantial methodological innovation or deeper insights into why/when the approach works

Significant gap remains to ground truth performance (PM predictor R²=0.9334 vs. StructRTL R²=0.8676 for area; R²=0.9484 vs. R²=0.8872 for delay), limiting practical utility without further improvements
Lack of justification for key hyperparameter choices (α=0.5, τ=0.7, μ=0.5, k=16 eigenvectors); no sensitivity analysis or ablation studies demonstrating their importance
No cross-dataset evaluation; dataset is synthetic/curated from GitHub and textbooks rather than industrial designs, raising questions about generalization and practical applicability
Missing analysis of interpretability, failure modes, and computational complexity; no comparison of inference time vs. LLM-based approaches despite claiming superiority
Insufficient investigation of edge prediction task design (why equal positive/negative samples?) and knowledge distillation design (why only final-layer activations?)

strengths: Well-motivated use of explicit CDFGs for capturing structural semantics in RTL designs, with clear advantages over implicit token-based representations
Thoughtful domain-aware adaptation of graph SSL techniques, particularly masking post-GNN embeddings to preserve computational integrity in CDFGs
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple baselines (graph-based and LLM-based), metrics, and ablation studies demonstrating importance of both pretraining tasks
Effective handling of severe class imbalance through stratified masking and class-balanced focal loss
Consistent performance improvements across all evaluation metrics (Tables 1-2), with especially notable gains for delay prediction (R² ~0.11 improvement over CodeV-QW-7B)
Clear presentation, detailed methodology, and commitment to code release supporting reproducibility
Addresses a practically important problem in hardware design automation with potential workflow impact
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: core techniques (masked modeling, edge prediction) are established graph SSL methods adapted from GraphMAE and MaskGAE; stratified masking and focal loss are well-known; KD strategy adopted from VeriDistill

Insufficient justification and ablation of key design choices: spectral positional embeddings lack domain-specific validation, hyperparameter values (α=0.5, τ=0.7, μ=0.5) appear arbitrary without sensitivity analysis

Modest empirical improvements over strongest LLM baseline in some metrics (~1% R² gain for area), and substantial gap remains to PM predictor teacher (0.9334 vs 0.8676), suggesting fundamental RTL-stage prediction limitations

Knowledge distillation requirement undermines practical benefits: achieving best performance requires synthesis pipeline (Yosys+ABC), negating claimed speedup over traditional flows; computational preprocessing costs not discussed

Shallow analysis of learned representations: no investigation of which structural patterns drive improvements, no case studies or failure analysis, limited justification beyond intuition for why CDFGs help

Experimental limitations: single dataset split without cross-dataset generalization testing, no out-of-distribution evaluation, no statistical significance testing or error bars, potential selection bias from filtering designs to synthesizable subset

Scalability and deployment concerns inadequately addressed: no analysis of how method scales to very large industrial designs (up to 19K+ nodes), inference latency/memory unspecified, unclear integration into actual EDA workflows

Missing ablations on critical design choices: edge prediction task difficulty not validated (95.77% accuracy suggests task may be too easy), no analysis of alternative masking strategies or positional embedding schemes
No experiments combining CDFG with LLM embeddings to isolate the value of structural information versus LLM features

strengths: Well-motivated approach leveraging structural semantics (CDFGs) over token-based views for RTL quality estimation with clear intuition about why this is superior
Domain-tailored pretraining tasks (structure-aware masked node modeling, edge prediction) thoughtfully adapted to preserve computational integrity of CDFGs while addressing class imbalance

Comprehensive experimental evaluation with large-scale dataset (13,200 designs vs. ~100 in prior work), multiple baselines, extensive ablation studies, and industrial validation achieving 145× speedup over synthesis
Strong and consistent empirical results across metrics with 0.1 R² improvement over prior SOTA (VeriDistill) for both area and delay prediction
Thorough presentation with clear figures, detailed implementation details, extensive appendices covering architectural ablations, sensitivity analysis, and generalization studies
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (GNN, Transformer, BERT-style masking, edge prediction) without fundamental innovation; knowledge distillation borrowed directly from VeriDistill

Severe practical limitations: (1) trained only on SkyWater 130nm—cannot generalize across technology nodes, (2) scalability issues with 52GB peak memory for 20K nodes, (3) notably weaker performance on sequential circuits (R² 0.7388 vs 0.7503), all of which limit real-world deployment

Dataset and evaluation concerns: training set includes LLM-generated designs of unclear quality, industrial evaluation limited to 51 design pairs, single random train/val split in main experiments shows degradation on functional/size-based splits (Appendices H-I)

Incomplete comparison with LLM baselines: frozen models don't reflect fair comparison; fine-tuning shows severe overfitting (val R²=0.2685 vs train R²=0.9915) but alternative fine-tuning strategies not explored

Significant technical issues: Equation 2 symmetrizes directed graphs as undirected losing directionality; Appendix N shows register-boundary partitioning (proposed scalability solution) degrades area ranking accuracy from 82.35% to 78.43%; lack of statistical rigor with no confidence intervals, significance testing, or cross-validation

Narrow scope and limited generalizability: specific to Yosys+ABC+SkyWater 130nm flow not validated on commercial tools or modern technology nodes; sequential circuit limitations unresolved; primarily addresses EDA-specific problem with limited interest for general ML venue
Knowledge distillation dependency: requires full synthesis to obtain PM netlists during training, reducing practical benefit; without KD, improvements are more modest

Insufficient analysis of why CDFG works better: limited empirical investigation of learned representations, no visualization or per-design analysis, qualitative discussion in Appendix L but lacking empirical backing

strengths: Well-motivated core insight: CDFGs explicitly encode structural semantics while token-based methods capture implicitly; particularly strong for delay prediction tied to design structure
Technically sound methodology with carefully justified design choices (post-GNN masking, stratified masking with class-balanced focal loss, spectral positional embeddings)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: extensive baseline comparisons, thorough ablations proving necessity of both pretraining tasks, generalization studies across functionality/size, industrial validation with 51 design pairs
Strong empirical results: ~0.1 R² improvement over SOTA without KD, 145× speedup over synthesis enabling practical iterative design workflows
Honest discussion of limitations: acknowledges sequential circuit performance gaps, scalability concerns, technology-node specificity, and provides detailed analysis in appendices

Reproducibility and practical impact: 13,200-design dataset, clear specifications, comprehensive appendices, industrial evaluation demonstrating real-world utility (82.35% area ranking, 88.23% delay ranking accuracy)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty for top-tier ML venue: masked node modeling and edge prediction are established SSL techniques; knowledge distillation borrowed from VeriDistill; main novelty is incremental adaptation (post-GNN vs. raw embedding masking)

Unresolved scalability challenges: memory reaches 52GB for 20K nodes; register-boundary partitioning (pilot tested) degrades area ranking accuracy 3.9% (78.43% vs 82.35%); unclear how method scales to 100K+ node industrial designs

Significant sequential circuit performance gap: R² drops 0.01-0.02 for sequential vs. combinational circuits; sequential circuits critical for real hardware but paper acknowledges without solving the fundamental limitation

Technology-node specificity limits generality: all experiments on SkyWater 130nm only; post-synthesis distributions shift across nodes; no experiments on other technology nodes (65nm, 28nm); requires retraining for deployment

Dataset composition raises concerns: 80.8% of designs <600 nodes; 61.6% <5000 nodes (training on simple designs); majority from LLM-generated sources (VeriGen, RTLCoder, MGVerilog); only 51 industrial pairs for evaluation (potential synthetic-data bias)

Hyperparameter choices lack ablation and justification: k=16 for Laplacian eigenvectors (no sensitivity study), α=0.5, τ=0.7, μ=0.5 appear arbitrary; minimum per-class m in stratified masking not specified in main text
Knowledge distillation benefit unclear: KD improves all methods including LLM baselines; paper doesn't isolate whether CDFG representation advantage or KD is primary contributor to performance gains
Statistical rigor absent: no error bars, confidence intervals, or multiple runs reported; single 0.8:0.2 train/val split; no statistical significance testing of performance differences

CDFG construction underspecified: limited detail on how complex RTL features (nested FSMs, memories, parameterized modules) map to nodes; no discussion of edge cases, completeness of extraction, or handling of unsynthesizable code
